metadata.verification_scope: Focused retest of original findings only; no broad security scan performed.

findings.title: Unsafe expression evaluation enables code execution
findings.pre_remediation: User-controlled expression data reached Python eval, allowing arbitrary code execution.
findings.post_remediation: The endpoint calls safe_eval_expression, which parses expressions with ast and permits only numeric constants, arithmetic operators, unary operators, and numeric expression nodes.
verification_evidence: Static scan found no eval( call in main.py.
Runtime check accepted '1 + 2 * 3' and rejected '__import__("os").system("id")' with unsupported-expression handling.

findings.title: OS command injection in DNS lookup
findings.pre_remediation: The address parameter was concatenated into a shell command and executed through popen.
findings.post_remediation: The shell execution helper rp raises unconditionally, and /lookup uses dns_lookup with strict host/IP character validation and socket.gethostbyname_ex rather than shell execution.
verification_evidence: Static scan found no popen import or call.
Runtime check submitted 'example.com; whoami' and received generic lookup failure without reflecting/executing the shell payload.

findings.title: Insecure pickle deserialization from cookie
findings.pre_remediation: The value cookie was base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads, allowing code execution through malicious pickle payloads.
findings.post_remediation: Cookie data is signed JSON using HMAC helpers; invalid or legacy pickle-shaped values are rejected before application use.
verification_evidence: Static scan found no pickle import or pickle.loads call.
Runtime check placed a base64 pickle in the value cookie and observed safe 'Invalid cookie' handling.

findings.title: Server-side template injection in greeting
findings.pre_remediation: The name parameter was interpolated into the Jinja template source before rendering, enabling template expression execution.
findings.post_remediation: The template source is static and user input is passed as a template variable.
verification_evidence: Static scan found no render_template_string(template) pattern using a user-built template string.
Runtime check submitted '{{7*7}}' and observed the literal payload, not evaluated output '49'.

findings.title: SQL injection in service listing filter
findings.pre_remediation: The category parameter was interpolated directly into the WHERE clause, allowing UNION-based extraction from secret_stuff.
findings.post_remediation: The WHERE clause uses a database-specific placeholder and cursor.execute receives user input as parameters.
verification_evidence: Static review found cursor.execute(query_build('SELECT * from public_stuff{}'.format(where)), tuple(params)).
Runtime check confirmed a normal products filter still returns expected data.
Runtime check submitted a UNION payload and did not expose secret table rows.
findings.validation_note: Runtime execution was verified with the sqlite path. Placeholder selection for oracle/sqlite/other DBs was statically reviewed.

findings.title: JWT algorithm confusion and None algorithm acceptance
findings.pre_remediation: Token verification accepted attacker-controlled algorithm choices including HS256 and None paths.
findings.post_remediation: ALLOWED_ALGORITHMS is RS256 only and the HS256/None helper paths are absent.
verification_evidence: Static scan confirmed ALLOWED_ALGORITHMS = ['RS256'] and no verify_token_none, verify_token_hs256, or create_token_hs256 helpers remain.
Runtime check confirmed a valid RS256 guest login still works.
Runtime check submitted an alg None admin token and received generic token-read failure; admin access was not granted.

findings.title: XML external entity processing
findings.pre_remediation: The XML parser allowed unsafe DTD/entity behavior that could resolve external entities.
findings.post_remediation: The parser is configured with no_network=True, load_dtd=False, dtd_validation=False, resolve_entities=False, and huge_tree=False.
verification_evidence: Static review confirmed the hardened XMLParser options.
Runtime check submitted a file:// XXE payload and observed the unresolved escaped entity without local file disclosure.

findings.title: Config oracle / encrypted config selector abuse
findings.pre_remediation: AES-CBC encrypted selector handling exposed distinguishable errors and allowed manipulation of config key selection.
findings.post_remediation: Config selectors are HMAC-signed JSON tokens and only app_* keys are viewable; tampering returns a generic invalid-key response.
verification_evidence: Static review confirmed make_config_token/read_config_token signed selector helpers.
Runtime check confirmed config listing still renders and a signed approved selector resolves.
Runtime check submitted a tampered selector and received generic 'Invalid config key' without padding/error details.

findings.title: Reflected/stored HTML injection across rendered values
findings.affected_area: Rendered cookie, lookup, evaluation, service, and user values
findings.pre_remediation: Multiple routes concatenated unescaped user-controlled or data-store-controlled values into HTML responses.
findings.post_remediation: HTML-rendered dynamic values are escaped with html.escape or rendered through Jinja variable escaping; error messages are generic in sensitive paths.
verification_evidence: Static review found html.escape applied in the remediated output paths.
Runtime cookie check submitted '<script>alert(1)</script>' and observed escaped output, not an executable script tag.
findings.validation_note: Focused verification covered representative original XSS paths and reviewed related output paths; no broad XSS fuzzing was performed.

findings.title: JWT private key material written to temporary predictable files
findings.pre_remediation: When key environment variables were absent, generated key material was written to temporary private/public key files and file paths were printed.
findings.post_remediation: Fallback key material is generated in memory and assigned directly to SIGN_KEY and VERIFY_KEY; no private/public key file paths are created.
verification_evidence: Static scan found no private.pem or public.pem references in main.py.
Import/startup message states in-memory temporary keys are generated when key files are not configured.

findings.title: Missing security attributes on sensitive cookies
findings.pre_remediation: Application cookies were set without HttpOnly/SameSite and without conditional Secure attributes.
findings.post_remediation: Both cookie-setting paths set httponly=True, samesite='Lax', and secure=request.is_secure.
verification_evidence: Static review confirmed both set_cookie calls include HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and request.is_secure-driven Secure behavior.
Runtime checks confirmed HttpOnly is present on the value cookie and authentication cookie.
findings.validation_note: Secure is intentionally conditional on HTTPS request context; production deployment must terminate HTTPS correctly for Secure cookies.

verification_commands: focused Flask test-client retest covering original abuse paths
